Parameterized SQL queries are safer than string concatenation because they prevent SQL injection, which can lead to security vulnerabilities such as injection attacks. This prevents malicious code from being executed, which can lead to information leakage or unauthorized access to data. Parameterized queries use placeholders that are replaced by actual values when the query is executed, which helps to prevent SQL injection by ensuring that only authorized data is processed. Additionally, using parameterized queries can improve performance by reducing the number of times the database needs to parse and execute the SQL query.

String concatenation can lead to SQL injection, where user input is directly embedded into the SQL query, potentially compromising the security of the database. Parameterized queries, which separate the SQL query from the data, prevent injection attacks by separating the data from the SQL code and ensuring that the data is treated as a separate set of characters.
